newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan says APEC has moved forward at Manila meet.
newsitem.headline: Japan says APEC has moved forward at Manila meet.

text.p: Japanese officials said on Saturday APEC had made progress towards its free-trade goals at this year's annual conference and had said a voluntary approach was a viable one.
But they conceded that Japan had enjoyed only limited success on its own APEC initiatives, which include a call to protect foreign investment in the region.

"The Individual Action Plans...submitted by all members as promised, mean that the so-called APEC method of voluntary measures works," Sumio Kusaka, chief of Japan's APEC desk at the Foreign Ministry, told reporters.

Kusaka and other Japanese trade officials said the plans from the 18 members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum amounted to an important first step toward the group's target of free trade and investment in the region by 2020. Individual plans allow each member to make voluntary commitments and move ahead at their own pace.
But the officials were less positive about Japan's own performance. "I would only give us a 70 percent grade," one senior Trade Ministry official said.

He said Japan met fierce opposition to its call for uniform rules to protect regional foreign investment. A joint statement issued by APEC ministers on Saturday only had a vague reference to "the increasing importance of investment" as a vehicle of economic growth in the region, where Japan is a key investor.
But Japan did win support for its proposal to coordinate export credit agencies, which often act as government-backed trade insurance agencies, to boost infrastructure investment.

Japanese officials were perplexed, however, over the wording in the joint statement regarding a U.S. proposal for scrapping tariffs on computers and related goods, called the Information Technology Agreement (ITA).
The United States has sought APEC's endorsement to help get the ITA approved at next month's meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore.
"....the ministers endorsed the efforts at the WTO to conclude an information technology agreement...," the statement said.
"We are not sure why the ITA is written in small letters because the only prts kind is the U.S. one," a senior Trade Ministry official said.
Malaysia and other developing countries said it was impossible to adopt the ITA at such short notice and that Japan and the United States should not push them into accepting it.
APEC leaders hold their annual summit on Monday at Subic Bay north of Manila.
